requirements.requirement: /srv/drop exists as a shared writable directory on node1 (all users can write into it)
requirements.summary: Directory created with mode 1777 (drwxrwxrwt), owner root:root, verified immediately after creation and confirmed still present with same mode/owner after a full reboot.

requirements.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users in /srv/drop
requirements.summary: Functional test showed dropuserA created a file and dropuserB's attempt to remove it failed with 'Operation not permitted' (exit 1), both before and after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: File owners (or root) can still remove their own files in the shared directory
requirements.summary: dropuserA successfully removed its own file both before and after the reboot, confirming the sticky bit only restricts removal of other users' files, not the owner's.

requirements.requirement: Configuration persists across a node restart (supplemental restart-evidence protocol, not explicit in task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id df76a1d0-6d86-4c46-a6b8-0a6b8156ab2f differs, confirming a genuine restart. /srv/drop retained mode/ownership and sticky-bit delete-restriction behavior was re-verified functionally afterward, showing a full baseline-disruption-recovery transition.

overall_summary: The executor configured /srv/drop on node1 with mode 1777 (drwxrwxrwt, root:root), satisfying the shared-writable-directory-with-sticky-bit requirement. Functional testing directly demonstrated that a non-owner cannot remove another user's file (Operation not permitted) while the owner can, both before and after a full node reboot, which also confirms the configuration persists across restart with a directly observed baseline-disruption-recovery transition (boot_id changed from 2fc81aed... to df76a1d0...). Minor hygiene issue: leftover mail spool files from userdel without -r, otherwise clean.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) on both before/after snapshots, so package-manager consistency could not be independently verified.
Minor leftover mail spool files for temporary test users (dropuserA/dropuserB) were not explicitly cleaned, though this has no bearing on the core task outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were closely tied to the task or its verification: directory creation/permissions (cmd-f3875286134d4209), temporary test users created twice for functional verification and removed each time via userdel (cmd-dc6a80694b5d491a, cmd-f35f4d5c2dd34aa8, and again inside cmd-8fdef7b2f490402c), test files created and removed within the same commands. Minor residue: userdel was run without -r, and stderr in cmd-8fdef7b2f490402c ('Creating mailbox file: File exists') indicates leftover /var/mail spool files for dropuserA/dropuserB from the first test pass were not cleaned up; this is bounded, low-risk residue with no security impact. The reboot itself was a deliberate, task-relevant action for the supplemental restart-evidence protocol, not an unnecessary mutation.
